Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to the current 0.35.0-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5021, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5cgq-3rg8-m6cv, https://go.dev/issue/79568, https://go.dev/cl/781220, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI. Read every published external-dns-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 33 builds, 0.20.0-r0 to the current 0.24.0-r5, each for x86_64 and aarch64; every download was checked against the checksum in the package index. Each package installs one file, the Go program /usr/bin/external-dns. Its Go build information lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.20.0-r3; v0.49.0 in 0.20.0-r4 to 0.21.0-r1; v0.50.0 in 0.21.0-r2 to 0.21.0-r3; v0.51.0 in 0.21.0-r4; v0.52.0 in 0.21.0-r5 to 0.21.0-r6; v0.53.0 in 0.21.0-r7 to 0.21.0-r9; v0.54.0 in 0.21.0-r10 to 0.21.0-r11; v0.55.0 in 0.21.0-r12 to 0.22.0-r1; v0.56.0 in 0.22.0-r2; v0.57.0 in 0.22.0-r3 to 0.23.0-r2; v0.58.0 in 0.23.0-r3 to 0.24.0-r5, so the module is below v0.52.0 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r4. The only golang.org/x/crypto packages with functions in the program are cryptobyte, md4, pbkdf2, pkcs12 and scrypt in every build, plus chacha20poly1305, sha3 or the initialisation function of the separate ssh/terminal package in some builds. So the vulnerable code is not present in any published build, including those that carry a module version before v0.52.0. The same reader finds runtime.main and main.main in every build, and lists knownhosts.New, (*hostKeyDB).check and the (*hostKeyDB).IsRevoked method value in a test program built for linux/amd64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0 that uses knownhosts.New as an SSH host key callback.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-42508 (GO-2026-5021, GHSA-5cgq-3rg8-m6cv): before golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0, the known_hosts callback in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/knownhosts checked a presented certificate's own key for an @revoked marker but not the CA key that signed it, so a certificate signed by a revoked CA key was still accepted. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 by commit f717e29 (CL 781220, "ssh/knownhosts: respect @revoked CA keys", which names CVE-2026-42508), whose only change outside tests is to ssh/knownhosts/knownhosts.go: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5021, https://go.dev/cl/781220, https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/f717e29698a271c548239ed56bf5dd9516d6f7e8, https://go.dev/issue/79568, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI. The Go vulnerability database lists (*hostKeyDB).IsRevoked in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/knownhosts as the vulnerable function. This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. We read every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64: 28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, each matching its repository index checksum, together with the golang-1.26-dev-dbgsym (28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18) and golang-1.26-dev-oci-config (28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18) packages built from the same source in that repository and the golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config (28 versions, 1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18) packages in the DHI Debian security repository, on both architectures. The Go source tree each golang-1.26-dev package installs vendors these golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor: chacha20, chacha20poly1305, cryptobyte, cryptobyte/asn1, internal/alias and internal/poly1305. golang.org/x/crypto/ssh and golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/knownhosts are not among them, and /usr/lib/go/src/cmd/vendor holds no golang.org/x/crypto package. No package has a file or directory under a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh path, which includes ssh/knownhosts. A Go function-table (pclntab) reader run on every Go program in the golang-1.26-dev packages (the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) finds no function in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh or its subpackages, and finds runtime.main in each. A byte search of every ELF file, which also catches inlined names and strings, finds no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh string of any kind. The golang-1.26-dev-dbgsym packages hold separate debug files for those programs, which carry the programs' symbol tables and no compressed sections; the byte search finds no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh string in them and finds runtime.main in each. The oci-config and fips-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. In test programs we built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.50.0 that call knownhosts.New, the same reader finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/knownhosts functions, including the (*hostKeyDB).IsRevoked-fm method-value wrapper into which (*hostKeyDB).IsRevoked is inlined, and the byte search finds the (*hostKeyDB).IsRevoked name. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/knownhosts takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.
